title: Structured log fanout with trace-affinity and tenant-safe routing
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a resilient structured-log fanout layer that preserves trace affinity, enforces tenant-safe routing, and supports dual-path replication to Loki and ELK. Goal is to reduce cross-tenant leakage, improve trace-to-log joins for latency/error dashboards, and provide backpressure signals when downstream sinks are congested.
context: Current ingest proxies perform coarse tenant sharding and emit enriched JSON, but we see: 1) lost trace joins when requests bounce across shards, 2) occasional tenant bleed when schema adapters misroute, and 3) lack of coordinated backpressure across Loki clusters and ES/Opensearch indexes. This ticket scopes a fanout router + affinity index + safe-routing rules to address those gaps and provide observability teams with stable trace linking for production dashboards.
goals: Preserve trace affinity so all log fragments for a single trace are consistently routed to the same ingest shard or logical partition
Add tenant-safe routing rules to prevent event leakage across tenant pipelines even during adapter upgrades
Implement a dual-path replicator that writes canonical structured JSON to Loki and a normalized view to ELK with configurable retention hints
Emit backpressure and health metrics (per-tenant and per-sink) so console can surface latency/error risk before SLA breach
Provide compatibility with existing KV cache IDs and existing correlation-id formats (traceparent, x-request-id)
Ship with migration plan and automated compatibility tests for schema adapters
acceptance_criteria: 99.9% of spans/log lines for synthetic test traces are routed with consistent shard affinity across 100k parallel traces
No cross-tenant events observed in a 24h stress run with mixed schema adapters (sampled validation)
Dual-path writes succeed for 99% of messages under nominal load; failures to one sink are retried independently and surfaced via metrics
Backpressure metrics available in console (per-tenant enqueue depth, sink error rate) and an alert threshold defined
Integration tests included in CI that validate trace joins in our latency dashboard (end-to-end trace->log correlation)
out_of_scope: Deep restructuring of existing schema adapters (only compatibility shims and feature flags). Long-term retention/archival policy changes in ELK will be handled in a separate ticket.
design_decisions: Affinity key will be computed as: hash(trace_id) XOR tenant_id_v4 then modulo N_shards. This balances per-tenant hot traces while enabling shard reassignment.
We will not attempt cross-sink atomic writes. Each sink is treated independently with best-effort replication and observability for eventual consistency.
Tenant isolation will be enforced at router boundary using allowlists and a small WASM-based adapter sandbox to drop/transform misclassified events.
Use protobuf for internal wire format between router and workers, keep external ingress as structured JSON to preserve existing integrations.
Backpressure propagated via a lightweight gRPC health stream and Prometheus metrics; console will read both to show per-tenant risk.
Feature gated: affinity and dual-path on by default for new tenants, opt-in for legacy tenants for 6 weeks before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Implement a new 'fanout-router' service with these components: ingress adapter, affinity-index, tenant-policy engine, per-sink dispatcher. Reuse existing KV cache library for low-latency lookups. Add a small Rust WASM sandbox for tenant schema checks. Provide a migration mode that records 'candidate-route' in logs for 1 week before switching live traffic.
tasks: Spec: affinity algorithm + shard reassignment plan
Prototype fanout-router (ingest->affinity->dispatch) with a single Loki sink
Add tenant-policy engine and WASM sandbox for adapter validation
Extend dispatcher to support ELK path and retention hints metadata
Instrument backpressure metrics and gRPC health stream
Write CI integration tests for trace-to-log joins and tenant-isolation
Create rollout plan and runbook for fallback during sink outages
Docs: Confluence design doc, Console runbook, and migration checklist
risks: Affinity hotspots: a single tenant or trace could overwhelm a shard — mitigated by dynamic shard splitting and short-circuiting large traces to a fanout bypass
WASM sandbox performance cost — mitigate with microbenchmarks and optional CPU pool quota per-tenant
Dual-path divergence creates confusion for SU teams — mitigate with reconciliation job and consumer-visible headers indicating canonical sequence IDs
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Deploy fanout-router in shadow mode; record candidate-route headers and compare with current router. Phase 2 (1 week): Enable per-tenant opt-in for affinity. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Gradual rollout for new tenants with monitoring thresholds. Phase 4: Force switch for legacy tenants after 6-week opt-in window, with rollback path to previous router.
monitoring_and_alerting: Prometheus metrics: fanout_router_queue_depth{tenant}, sink_error_rate{sink,tenant}, affinity_mismatch_rate. Console: Add per-tenant dashboard tiles for enqueue depth and recent affinity reassignments. Alert: sink_error_rate > 5% for 5m -> P1 paging
